innovations.agent_role: The Agent proposes and replans schedules; deterministic gates evaluate them; human governance freezes accepted scope.
innovations.competition_relevance: Combines explainable Agent assistance with an implementation-facing collective schedule contract and frozen evidence gates.
innovations.deterministic_validation: Python/C schedule parity, schema and invariant audits, frozen simulator comparison, and offline trace replay.
innovations.problem: Collective selection must expose auditable topology, chunking, dependency, and cost decisions instead of hiding them inside a monolithic algorithm call.
innovations.technical_mechanism: A shared Schedule IR v2 carries phases and reliability metadata into topology-aware schedule generation, selector scoring, deterministic evaluation, and replanning.
innovations.title: Topology-aware Schedule IR optimization pipeline

innovations.agent_role: The Agent supplies proposals and reflections; deterministic evaluators and explicit human gates control decisions.
innovations.competition_relevance: Makes Agent contribution reproducible and defensible while retaining explicit human governance and negative feature gates.
innovations.deterministic_validation: Mandatory offline replay verifies hashes, schemas, decision flow, human-intervention fields, and frozen source pointers without API keys.
limitations: normalized traces are not hidden chain-of-thought
innovations.problem: Agent proposals are difficult to trust when proposal, evaluation, human intervention, and evidence provenance are not separable.
innovations.technical_mechanism: Normalized proposal/evaluation/reflection/replanning records map prompts and skills through deterministic gates to sources, commits, evidence, figures, and claim boundaries.
innovations.title: Evidence-governed Agent optimization and feature loop

innovations.agent_role: The Agent feature loop proposed sparse delivery and recorded its evidence-gated implementation decision.
innovations.competition_relevance: Adds an auditable, lossless communication reduction path while explicitly rejecting unprofitable sparse encodings.
innovations.deterministic_validation: Host-executed correctness/parity cases plus frozen logical byte, compression-ratio, and break-even accounting.
limitations: wire bytes are modeled/logical accounting, not NIC measurement
sparse path is not real-device validated
innovations.problem: Sparse communication can add index overhead and lose value unless density, encoding, reconstruction, and dense fallback share one accounting boundary.
innovations.technical_mechanism: A lossless index/value codec, sparse reconstruction, modeled wire-byte accounting, break-even decision, and dense fallback integrate with collective and schedule paths.
innovations.title: Lossless sparse collective path with wire-aware fallback

innovations.agent_role: The feature Agent proposed reliability work; deterministic gates split implemented host semantics from simulator-only backpressure.
innovations.competition_relevance: Provides a precise reliability story whose evidence identity remains visible at every layer.
innovations.deterministic_validation: C/Python CRC parity, corruption injection/detection, retry recovery/exhaustion cases, and simulated credit-window scenarios.
limitations: no NIC or HCCL hardware reliability validation
backpressure is simulated rather than host-runtime executed
innovations.problem: Reliability claims become misleading when host corruption checks, retry policy, and simulator flow control are blended into one hardware claim.
innovations.technical_mechanism: CRC32 sequence/chunk integrity metadata and retry budgets execute on host paths, while credit/backpressure semantics remain a Schedule IR and simulator layer.
innovations.title: Layered integrity, retry, and backpressure contract

innovations.agent_role: Agent and report layers describe capability boundaries; no runtime Agent action invokes ACL/HCCL in the mandatory path.
innovations.competition_relevance: Balances portable submission verification with an explicit production integration source path and honest hardware boundary.
innovations.deterministic_validation: Linux CPU_SIM ABI/CTest/pytest validation plus Direct declaration, expression, compile, link, and lifecycle readiness checks.
innovations.problem: A submission plugin needs reproducible CPU validation while retaining a credible path toward official ACL/HCCL integration without pretending hardware execution.
innovations.technical_mechanism: The frozen CPU_SIM plugin preserves SONAME and 19-symbol ABI; a default-OFF Direct adapter expresses official calls and supports compile/link/lifecycle readiness artifacts.
innovations.title: Layered CPU_SIM ABI and Direct production readiness

novelty_claim_policy: No first, unique, industry-leading, production-ready, or hardware-validated claim is asserted.
